question: When difference between compound and simple interest for three years is ₹155 at 10% interest per annum, the principal is ₹______
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective SI for 3 years at 10% = 10% × 3 = 30%

Effective CI for 3 years at 10% = 33.1%

Difference in % = 33.1% − 30% = 3.1%

According to the question, 3.1% of Principal = ₹155

⇒ Principal = (155 ÷ 3.1) × 100 = ₹5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between CI and SI (D) = ₹155

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

For 3 years, the difference between CI and SI is:

D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (300 + R) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 155 = P × (10 ÷ 100)² × (300 + 10) ÷ 100

⇒ 155 = P × (1 ÷ 100) × (310 ÷ 100)

⇒ 155 = P × 0.01 × 3.1

⇒ 155 = P × 0.031

⇒ P = 155 ÷ 0.031

⇒ P = ₹5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years on a certain principal P at rate R% is given by the formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Effective Rate Method for 3 years

Effective Compound Interest rate for 3 years at 10% p.a. is 33.1%, whereas Simple Interest is exactly 30%. The percentage difference will strictly be 3.1% of the principal amount.

Effective Rate Formula

For 2 years, the effective CI = 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%. For 3 years, the effective CI = 3R + (3R² ÷ 100) + (R³ ÷ 10000)%.
